questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The environment, and the nature of Australia.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go see the wild kangaroos at Jervis Bay. And pet them.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UNSW was very helpful towards exchange students, and students un general. They always had open doors at the nucleus for meetings with councilors. 10/10

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an opening day, and a first course was specifically designed for exchange students. The teachers and the faculty took care of us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult to find housing. Reccomendation: Live on Campus if possible. Search early, and look before you are even accepted into the program or have a visa.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive, and transport costs will make it the same price as living closer to campus or on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They always helped us sign up for courses. I needed to exchange a course 2 weeks in, and it was no issue, unlike at KU.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: registration was easy. Just find the courses online, enter them on MyUNSW. Just remember courses tend to fill up, so enter early.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help at the Nucleus (Student councilling hub)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got everything i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The only issue is KU, not UNSW. KU are rude and dont want to offer help or merit. UNSW are kind helpful, and will make anything work. They had a sufficient number of staff.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: High level, good quality education.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Courses were appropriate for their level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More hands on at UNSW. The teachers also want to interact with the students. At KU the teachers are often divorced from the students and do not know or care for them. At UNSW you will get to know the teachers and make friendships with them.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Nutrition, An Introduction to the Sydney Environment, Context of Health Data Science, Introduction to Film Studies.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: An Introduction to the Sydney Environment. Take this course in the Summer. You get to learn about Sydney and Australia. PLEASE take this course. It offloads some of the ECTS early. You get to go on field trips, socialize with other exchange students, and the teachers are amazing and kind.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: VISA costed 8000 DKK. Please consider this before travelling.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive in Sydney.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many clubs and fun activities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: EVERYTHING. I partook in the D&D club, and the Alt fashion society. But there is literally anything you want. HUGE selection, just come to the O-week and you'll see all the booths.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: D&D club for the nerds.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Jervis bay Beach to see the wild kangaroos.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to people you meet in class and ask them to go places with you. Zoo or beach or adventure. You are on exchange, take initiative, if it goes wrong they wont remember you, as youll be gone in 6 months.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Helpfulness and kindness. People are sociable and always want to help you. They never scoff at you, or are rude in public. People want to help always.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. MAKE SURE YOU GET A PLACE TO LIVE, FAST (and yes it will be EXPENSIVE)
2. Go see things, and don't worry about your grades. Just go on adventures.
3. Take the "An introduction to the Sydney Environment" Course

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hand in assignments late. There is a 5% penalty. That might not sound like a lot. But its not a penalty on your assignement, its a penalty off your final grade in the subject! so please never hand in anything late.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making an Australian friend. Thank you Mila <3.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
